problem: VLA navigation models depend on scarce, labor-intensive robot data and static image-text backbones that cannot capture temporal dynamics or physics; prior video-model navigation work used future-frame prediction only as an auxiliary signal and was limited to constrained benchmarks such as image-goal navigation.
motivation: Internet-scale video models encode spatiotemporal and physical priors, and video can serve as a unified state-action interface across platforms. Navigation needs mostly high-level directional decisions rather than precise low-level actions, which makes it a natural fit for video-based planning.
key_idea: Use a pretrained generative video model as a zero-shot high-level navigation planner: sample K videos from an image and instruction, pick the best with a VLM judge, then decode metric waypoints with pi^3 and Moge2 scale recovery, and execute them with Ego-Planner.
insight: Sampling more candidates and selecting with a VLM raises task success, so the stochasticity of video generation can be handled with best-of-K selection. pi^3 recovers only about 46% of the true scale outdoors, and Moge2 median scale calibration cuts the relative error to about 10%. Prompt detail matters most: decomposed, timed sub-event prompts raise task completion from 0.41 (simple) to 0.73, while automatic rewriting reaches only 0.58.
method: Video generation: a pretrained image-to-video model (Wan 2.6 via API in the real-world system) synthesizes a first-person navigation video from the current RGB image and the instruction.

Generative sampling optimization: K candidate videos are generated. Qwen3-VL first applies a binary pass/fail filter (task-consistent and collision-free). It then scores action safety, scene consistency and task performance, and the best video is chosen by argmax of R = 0.8*as + 0.8*sc + 1.4*tp. If no candidate is valid, a human decides whether to resample.
Waypoint decoding (IDM): the chosen video is downsampled into frames, and pi^3 recovers camera poses (x, y, z, yaw) and local pointmaps.

Metric scale recovery: Moge2 gives metric reference depth. A mask keeps pixels with reference depth in 0.5-30 m and positive pi^3 depth. The global scale is the median of the per-pixel D_ref/Z_pred ratios, and waypoints are multiplied by it.

Low-level planner: Ego-Planner tracks the waypoints with real-time obstacle avoidance, advancing to the next waypoint once within a distance threshold. Max velocity and acceleration are set from the video's dynamics, and yaw is controlled independently.

Benchmark: 15 tasks in 5 categories (object navigation, precise navigation, spatial grounding, language control, scene reasoning), scored by UAV pilots on visual consistency, dynamic feasibility and task completion.
Real deployment: RealSense camera, LiDAR with Fast-LIVO2 for pose, decoder on a laptop, planner on a Jetson Orin NX.

setting.backbone: Wan 2.6 (closed, frozen, API) for real-world use; Wan 2.2 I2V 14B, HunyuanVideo-1.5 8B, Cosmos-Predict 2.5 14B and LVP compared; Qwen3-VL as VLM judge; pi^3 + Moge2 for decoding
setting.training_data: none (training-free, zero-shot; all components are pretrained)
setting.observation: single monocular RGB image plus text instruction; LiDAR/IMU for pose and obstacle mapping in the low-level planner
setting.action_space: 3D waypoints (x, y, z, yaw) executed by Ego-Planner as continuous collision-free trajectories on a UAV
setting.privileged: none (a human supervisor is consulted only when no valid sample exists)

numbers.eval_set_note: 15 tasks, 5 samples per task per model, scored by UAV pilots
numbers.extra: Table scores are means of 5 independent samples, without the sampling-optimization stage; human pilot scoring

numbers.eval_set_note: 6 challenging tasks, 5 samples each, Wan 2.6, prompt ablation

numbers_note: No standard benchmarks reported. The sampling-budget ablation and the scale-error results appear only in figures (scale error about 46% of ground truth reduced to about 10% relative error, per the text). No real-world success-rate table is given.
results: Wan 2.6 is the best video backbone, with average task completion 0.84 versus 0.48 for Wan 2.2, 0.45 for Hunyuan 1.5 and 0.13 for Cosmos 2.5 and LVP. The system shows zero-shot indoor and outdoor UAV flight. A larger sampling budget improves success, and decomposed prompts reach 0.73 task completion versus 0.41 for simple prompts.
limitations: Poor at high-agility or high-precision maneuvers such as aerobatics and traversing narrow hoops.
Generating a video takes 1-2 minutes via API, which rules out reactive or real-time use.

Video models show pattern bias, reward hacking, mode collapse and instruction neglect; the benchmark uses human pilot scoring on a small set of 15 tasks with only 5 samples each, and there are no comparisons to prior navigation methods.
